questions.question: On average, a courier delivers a parcel every three minutes. At that rate, how long will it take the courier to deliver 73 parcels?
questions.answer: $73 \times 3 = 219$ minutes $= 3$ hours $39$ minutes. **(B)**

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of an equation. Which of the following equations does the graph best represent?
questions.answer: The curve has a positive $y$-intercept, is decreasing and approaches the $x$-axis (an exponential decay). $y = 2^{-x}$ has $y$-intercept $1$ and decreases towards $0$. The reciprocal graphs $y = \pm\frac{2}{x}$ have no $y$-intercept, and $y = 2^x$ is increasing. **(C)**

questions.question: A map of a particular city has a scale of $1 : 50\,000$. If the distance between Jesse's home and the airport is 4 centimetres on this map, what is the actual distance?
The diagram shows the locations of two towns, Alhambra and Brentwood. What is the bearing of Brentwood from Alhambra?
questions.answer: Alhambra is on a bearing of $120^\circ$ clockwise from north to the line AB... in the diagram, $120^\circ$ is the angle at Alhambra between north and the direction to Brentwood measured round through the south-west? The line to Brentwood is $60^\circ$ from the south direction, towards the west. So Brentwood is S$60^\circ$W from Alhambra. **(C)**

questions.question: Consider the linear equations $y = x + 2$ and $y = 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}x$. Which diagram could be used to find the solution to these simultaneous linear equations?
questions.answer: Both lines have $y$-intercept $2$. The first has gradient $+1$ (rising) and the second has gradient $-\frac{1}{2}$ (falling). Only diagram A shows one rising line and one falling line crossing at $(0, 2)$. **(A)**

questions.question: Consider the network diagram. What is the sum of the degrees of all the vertices shown on the network diagram?
questions.answer: The network has 6 edges and the sum of the degrees is twice the number of edges: $2 \times 6 = 12$. (Degrees: $A = 2$, $B = 2$, $C = 1$, $D = 3$, $E = 4$.) **(D)**

questions.question: A set of bivariate data has a Pearson's correlation coefficient of $-0.95$. Which expression best describes the association between the two variables?
questions.answer: $r = -0.95$ is close to $-1$, so the association is strong and negative. **(B)**
options: There is a weak negative association
There is a strong negative association
There is a weak positive association
There is a strong positive association

questions.question: A teacher asked fifty students to identify their favourite type of pet. A partially completed Pareto chart shows some of the data collected. How many students chose cats as their favourite pet?
questions.answer: The cumulative percentage rises from $40\%$ (dogs) to $68\%$ (dogs and cats), so cats are $68 - 40 = 28\%$ of the students. $28\% \times 50 = 14$ students. **(B)**

questions.question: Adam takes out a loan of \$10 000 to buy a new car. Simple interest is charged on the loan. To repay the loan and the interest charged, Adam makes payments of \$1200 every year over the next 10 years. What is the simple interest rate, per annum, that is charged on the loan?
questions.answer: Total repaid $= 1200 \times 10 = \$12\,000$, so the interest is $12\,000 - 10\,000 = \$2000$. $I = Prn$: $2000 = 10\,000 \times r \times 10 \Rightarrow r = 0.02 = 2\%$. **(A)**

questions.question:
Savannah competed in four throwing events at the district athletics carnival. In each event the distances recorded by the competitors were normally distributed.

| | Savannah's result | Event mean | Event standard deviation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shot put | 15 m | 13 m | 2 m |
| Discus | 37 m | 43 m | 6 m |
| Javelin | 57 m | 47 m | 8 m |
| Hammer throw | 33 m | 48 m | 10 m |

Which was Savannah's weakest event compared with the other competitors?
questions.answer: Compare $z$-scores: shot put $\frac{15 - 13}{2} = 1$; discus $\frac{37 - 43}{6} = -1$; javelin $\frac{57 - 47}{8} = 1.25$; hammer throw $\frac{33 - 48}{10} = -1.5$. The lowest $z$-score is the hammer throw. **(D)**

questions.question: Tennis players are allowed to serve the ball to their opponent up to two consecutive times. If the first serve is successful, the ball goes into play and a second serve is not performed. If the first serve is unsuccessful, the player will serve the ball a second time. Nava is a tennis player. The probability that her first serve is successful is 50% and the probability that her second serve is successful is 90%. What is the probability that Nava serves the ball successfully?
questions.answer: $P(\text{success}) = P(\text{first serve in}) + P(\text{first fails and second in}) = 0.5 + 0.5 \times 0.9 = 0.95 = 95\%$. **(D)**

questions.question: Charlotte is thinking of a number. Let the number be $x$. When Charlotte subtracts 6 from this number and multiplies the result by 4, the answer is 3 more than $x$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.answer: Subtract 6 and then multiply by 4: $4(x - 6)$. This equals 3 more than $x$: $x + 3$. So $4(x - 6) = x + 3$. **(C)**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fee or charge associated with using a credit card?
questions.answer: Interest, cash advance fees and late payment fees are all charged on credit cards; there is no "repayment fee". **(D)**

questions.question: The graph shows the depth of water in a container over time, as it is being filled. Which of the containers shown could reflect the graph above?
questions.answer: Water is poured in at a steady rate. The depth rises quickly at first (narrow base), then slowly (wide middle section), then quickly again (narrow neck). That is the round flask with a narrow neck. **(B)**

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, left their respective homes one morning and cycled along the same road. The graph shows their journeys (distance from home against time). Which of the friends made a stop first?
questions.answer: Shay. Her graph is horizontal (she stops, at 30 km) from 12 noon to 1 pm, before Mika stops at 45 km from 1 pm to 2 pm.

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, cycled along the same road, as shown in the graph. When Mika began cycling home, how far had Shay travelled on her trip?
questions.answer: Mika begins cycling home at 2 pm. By then Shay has cycled out $30$ km and back $20$ km (she is $10$ km from home), so she has travelled $30 + 20 = 50$ km.

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, cycled along the same road, as shown in the graph. What was Mika's average speed, to the nearest km/h, on the cycling trip?
questions.answer: Mika cycled from 10 am to 5 pm, which is $7$ hours, and travelled $45 + 45 = 90$ km. Average speed $= \dfrac{90}{7} \approx 13$ km/h.

questions.question: The flight time from Sydney to Dubai is approximately 13 hours. The Universal Coordinated Time of Dubai is $+4$ and Sydney is $+10$. A plane departs Sydney local time at 11:00 PM Sunday for Dubai. At what local time in Dubai is the plane expected to land?
questions.answer:
Dubai is $10 - 4 = 6$ hours behind Sydney, so the departure is 5:00 PM Sunday Dubai time. Adding the flight time of 13 hours gives $5{:}00\ \text{PM} + 13\ \text{h} = 6{:}00$ AM **Monday** in Dubai.

(Equivalently: arrive 12:00 noon Monday Sydney time, which is 6:00 AM Monday in Dubai.)

questions.question: A manager oversees four teenage employees working in a fast-food restaurant. The number of weeks they have been working at the restaurant, $x$, and the number of times they need to ask the manager for assistance during a four-hour shift, $y$, are shown on the graph: $(2, 15)$, $(6, 10)$, $(10, 6)$, $(17, 3)$. Find the equation of the least-squares regression line for the data set, finding the gradient and $y$-intercept correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Using the statistics mode of a calculator: gradient $= -0.79$ and $y$-intercept $= 15.38$.

$$y = 15.38 - 0.79x$$

questions.question: For four employees, the least-squares regression line for the number of times $y$ they need to ask for assistance during a four-hour shift against the number of weeks $x$ they have worked is $y = 15.38 - 0.79x$. Using this line as a guide, on average how many full weeks will an employee have to be working at the restaurant before they require assistance less than 8 times during a four-hour shift?
questions.answer:
$$15.38 - 0.79x < 8 \Rightarrow 0.79x > 7.38 \Rightarrow x > 9.34\ldots$$

(The paper's working uses $x > 9.38$ from the same rounded line.) So an employee needs to work $x > 9.3$ weeks, i.e. **10 full weeks**.

questions.question: The diagram shows a rectangular park that contains 3 triangular grass areas (shaded). There is a footpath (unshaded) around the edges of the park and between the grassed areas. The corners of the park are $A$, $B$, $C$, $E$ and $D$ is the point on the bottom edge where the two diagonal paths meet. Draw a network diagram to represent the possible walking paths through the park.
questions.answer: Vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ with edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EA$ (the outside path) and $AD$, $BD$ (the two diagonal paths).

questions.question: A network has vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ and edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EA$, $AD$, $BD$. Show that the sum of the degrees of the vertices is equal to twice the number of edges.
questions.answer:
| Vertex | $A$ | $B$ | $C$ | $D$ | $E$ | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Degree | 3 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 2 | 14 |

There are $7$ edges and $2 \times 7 = 14$, which equals the sum of the degrees.

questions.question:
A company purchases office furniture for \$10 000. The company accountant is considering two methods of depreciation:
- straight-line depreciation with the office furniture being depreciated by \$$D$ each year
- declining-balance depreciation at a rate of 15% per year

The accountant determines that after two years, the salvage value of the office furniture will be the same using either depreciation method. What is the value of $D$?
questions.answer:
Declining balance: $S = 10\,000(1 - 0.15)^2 = \$7225$. The depreciation after two years is $10\,000 - 7225 = \$2775$.

Straight line: $2D = 2775 \Rightarrow D = \$1387.50$.

questions.question: Two right-angled triangles, $ABD$ and $BCD$, are shown. In triangle $ABD$, $AB = 13$ cm and $AD = 12$ cm, and $\theta = \angle BAD$. Find the value of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{12}{13} \Rightarrow \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right) = 22.6^\circ \approx 23^\circ$.

questions.question: Two right-angled triangles, $ABD$ and $BCD$, are shown. In triangle $ABD$, $AB = 13$ cm and $AD = 12$ cm. In triangle $BCD$, $\angle BCD = 50^\circ$ and $BC = x$. Find the value of $x$, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
By Pythagoras in $\triangle ABD$: $BD^2 = 13^2 - 12^2 = 25 \Rightarrow BD = 5$ cm.

In $\triangle BCD$: $\sin 50^\circ = \dfrac{5}{x} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{5}{\sin 50^\circ} = 6.5$ cm.

questions.question: A 44-gallon drum has a base but no lid. The drum is 88 cm in height and has a diameter of 58 cm. The inside of the drum and the curved surface of the outside of the drum are to be painted. Underneath the base of the drum is not to be painted as it is in contact with the ground. What is the surface area to be painted, in square centimetres, correct to 1 decimal place?
questions.answer:
Radius $= 29$ cm.

- Inside: curved surface $2\pi(29)(88)$ plus base $\pi(29)^2$
- Outside: curved surface $2\pi(29)(88)$

Total $= 4\pi(29)(88) + \pi(29)^2 = 32\,069.4 + 2642.1 = 34\,711.5\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.question: The time it takes for a cupcake at a picnic to be eaten by ants ($t$ minutes) varies inversely with the number of ants eating the cupcake ($N$ ants). When there are 10 ants, the cupcake is eaten in 120 minutes. The equation relating $t$ and $N$ is $t = \dfrac{k}{N}$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: $120 = \dfrac{k}{10} \Rightarrow k = 1200$.

questions.question: The time it takes for a cupcake at a picnic to be eaten by $N$ ants is $t = \dfrac{1200}{N}$ minutes. Calculate how long it will take 20 ants to eat one cupcake.
questions.answer: $t = \dfrac{1200}{20} = 60$ minutes (1 hour).

questions.question:
The table shows the fat and calorie content of 12 different burgers on a fast-food restaurant's menu. Two of the values are missing and are represented by the letters $A$ and $B$.

| Fat (g) | 9 | 12 | 15 | 18 | 23 | 24 | 26 | 27 | 29 | $A$ | 31 | 43 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calories | 250 | $B$ | 320 | 380 | 420 | 420 | 515 | 530 | 545 | 600 | 620 | 750 |

The bivariate data is displayed in the scatter plot. Using the scatter plot, determine the values of $A$ and $B$.
questions.answer: The point with $600$ calories on the scatter plot is at $29$ g of fat, so $A = 29$. The point at $12$ g of fat has $300$ calories, so $B = 300$.

questions.question: A table and scatter plot show the fat content (g) and the calorie content of 12 different burgers. Identify the dependent variable.
questions.answer: Calories (the calorie content depends on the fat content).

questions.question: Anaya is paid \$38 per hour for the first 40 hours each week, with time-and-a-half for any overtime hours. In a particular week, Anaya earned \$285 in overtime. How many hours in total did she work that week?
questions.answer:
Overtime rate $= 1.5 \times 38 = \$57$ per hour, so the overtime hours are $\dfrac{285}{57} = 5$.

Total hours worked $= 40 + 5 = 45$ hours.

questions.question: Takeshi is considering two payment plans offered by an online music service. Plan A has a monthly subscription fee of \$3 and \$0.25 per song downloaded. Plan B has no monthly subscription fee and \$0.40 per song downloaded. Let $x$ be the number of songs downloaded and \$$C$ be the total cost per month. Write an equation that represents the monthly cost of Plan A.

Plan A costs $C = 0.25x + 3$ per month, where $x$ is the number of songs downloaded. The graph shows the line of the equation for the monthly cost of Plan B ($C = 0.40x$). On the graph, draw the line of the equation for Plan A.
questions.answer: Plot points such as $(0, 3)$, $(8, 5)$, $(20, 8)$ and $(28, 10)$, and join them with a straight line starting at $(0, 3)$ with gradient $0.25$. It crosses the Plan B line at $(20, 8)$.

questions.question: Plan A costs $C = 0.25x + 3$ and Plan B costs $C = 0.40x$ per month for $x$ songs. The two lines intersect at $(20, 8)$. Explain how Takeshi can decide which plan to select.
questions.answer: The lines intersect at $x = 20$ songs (cost \$8). If Takeshi downloads fewer than 20 songs a month, Plan B's line is lower, so Plan B is cheaper. If he downloads more than 20 songs, Plan A is cheaper. At exactly 20 songs the plans cost the same.

questions.question:
Roco has a credit card with the following conditions:
- There is no interest-free period.
- Interest is charged at the end of each month at 19.99% per annum, compounding daily, from the purchase date (included) to the last day of the month (included).

Roco's credit card statement for March (1 March to 31 March) shows: opening balance \$0.00; 19 March, car repairs, \$1200.00; 27 March, trailer hire, \$110.00; 31 March, interest charged, ***; 31 March, closing balance, ***. The minimum payment is calculated as 2.5% of the closing balance on 31 March. What will be the value of his minimum payment?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{0.1999}{365}$.

The \$1200 purchase is charged from 19 to 31 March, which is $13$ days, and the \$110 purchase from 27 to 31 March, which is $5$ days.

Closing balance $= 1200\left(1 + \dfrac{0.1999}{365}\right)^{13} + 110\left(1 + \dfrac{0.1999}{365}\right)^{5} = \$1318.87$.

Minimum payment $= 2.5\% \times 1318.87 = \$32.97$.

questions.question: The diagram shows a wheel of cheese with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 3 cm. A wedge representing one eighth of the cheese has been cut and removed from the wheel. Find the volume of the remaining cheese wheel, correct to the nearest cubic centimetre.
questions.answer: $V = \dfrac{7}{8} \times \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{7}{8} \times \pi (5)^2 (3) = 206.2 \approx 206\ \text{cm}^3$.

questions.question: The diagram represents a network with weighted edges. Draw a minimum spanning tree for this network and determine its length.
questions.answer:
Add the shortest edges that do not form a cycle: $CD = 2$, $ED = 3$, $BC = 4$, $FE = 6$. Then $AB = 8$ (the next shortest edge, $BE = 7$, would form a cycle).

The tree has edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$ and length $8 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 23$.

questions.question: The diagram represents a network with weighted edges. A new edge from $B$ to $F$ is added with a weight of $x$, where $x$ is a whole number. If the shortest path from $F$ to $D$ uses this new edge, what is the maximum value of $x$?
questions.answer:
The current shortest path from $F$ to $D$ is $F - E - D$ with length $6 + 3 = 9$.

Using the new edge, the shortest route is $F - B - C - D$ with length $x + 4 + 2 = x + 6$. For this to be the shortest path, $x + 6 < 9$, so $x < 3$.

The maximum whole-number value is $x = 2$.

questions.question: A spinner is divided into three sections $A$, $B$ and $C$. The sizes of the sections are $A$: $(7x + 10)^\circ$, $B$: $90^\circ$ and $C$: $3x^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.answer: The angles in a full turn sum to $360^\circ$: $7x + 10 + 90 + 3x = 360 \Rightarrow 10x = 260 \Rightarrow x = 26$.

questions.question: A spinner has three sections: $A$ with $(7x + 10)^\circ$, $B$ with $90^\circ$ and $C$ with $3x^\circ$, where $x = 26$. If the spinner is spun 60 times, how many times would it be expected to land on $C$?
questions.answer:
Section $C$ is $3 \times 26 = 78^\circ$, so $P(C) = \dfrac{78}{360}$.

Expected number $= 60 \times \dfrac{78}{360} = 13$ times.

questions.question: Shareen buys a car for \$29 000 and repays it over 4 years through equal monthly instalments. She pays a 10% deposit and interest is charged at 9% p.a. on the reducing balance loan. Using the table of present value interest factors, where $r$ represents the monthly interest rate and $N$ represents the number of payments, calculate the monthly repayment, \$$P$, that Shareen must pay to complete the loan after 4 years (to the nearest dollar).
questions.answer:
Deposit $= 0.10 \times 29\,000 = \$2900$, so the amount borrowed is $\$26\,100$.

$N = 4 \times 12 = 48$ and $r = \dfrac{9\%}{12} = 0.75\% = 0.0075$. The table factor is $40.18478$.

$P \times 40.18478 = 26\,100 \Rightarrow P = \dfrac{26\,100}{40.18478} = \$649$ (to the nearest dollar).

questions.question:
Gavin, a 72 kg male, consumes 4 bottles of beer at a party, each containing 1.4 standard drinks. Gavin started drinking his first beer at 8:20 PM and finished his 4th beer at 11:50 PM. The blood alcohol content (BAC) for males can be estimated by
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks, $H$ is the number of hours drinking and $M$ is the mass in kilograms. Calculate Gavin's BAC when he finished his fourth beer, correct to 3 decimal places.

A farmer has two flocks of chickens. The number of eggs they laid each day during the year was counted, with the data shown in a parallel box plot (Flock 1: minimum 4, $Q_1 = 7$, median 11, $Q_3 = 15$, maximum 18; Flock 2: minimum 6, $Q_1 = 8$, median 10, $Q_3 = 16$, maximum 20). Compare the two data sets, examining the skewness of the distributions, and any relevant measures of central tendency and spread.
questions.answer:
- **Centre:** Flock 1 has a higher median (11 eggs per day compared with 10).
- **Shape:** Flock 1 is approximately symmetrical (the median is in the middle of the box and the whiskers are about equal), while Flock 2 is positively skewed (the median is closer to $Q_1$ and the upper whisker is longer).
- **Spread:** The two flocks have the same range ($18 - 4 = 14$ and $20 - 6 = 14$) and the same interquartile range ($15 - 7 = 8$ and $16 - 8 = 8$).

questions.question: In the diagram, $\triangle PQR$ is similar to $\triangle STR$, $PQ = 45$ cm, $ST = 15$ cm, $QT = y$ and $TR = x$. Show that $y = 2x$.
questions.answer:
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are in the same ratio, so
$$\frac{QR}{TR} = \frac{PQ}{ST} \Rightarrow \frac{x + y}{x} = \frac{45}{15} = 3.$$
Then $x + y = 3x$, so $y = 2x$.

questions.question:
The table shows the income tax rates for the 2025–2026 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|---|---|
| \$0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000 |

For the 2025–2026 financial year, Amani has a taxable income of \$126 250. During the year she paid \$1130 per fortnight in Pay As You Go (PAYG) tax. Calculate Amani's tax refund, ignoring the Medicare levy.

120 people entered the first round of a crossword competition. The times taken to complete the crossword correctly were normally distributed with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 2.1 minutes. Approximately how many of the 120 correctly completed their crosswords in more than 12.1 minutes?
questions.answer:
$12.1 = 10 + 2.1$, so $z = 1$. About $68\%$ lie within one standard deviation, leaving $16\%$ above $z = 1$.

$0.16 \times 120 = 19.2 \approx 19$ people.

questions.question: The times taken to complete a crossword were normally distributed with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 2.1 minutes. If a competitor completed her crossword in 13.15 minutes, what was her $z$-score?

The table shows the future values of an annuity of \$1. At the end of each year, Albert deposits \$6000 into a bank account that earns interest at a rate of 4% per annum, compounding annually. He makes these contributions over a period of 20 years. How much interest will the account have earned after 20 years?
questions.answer:
From the table, 20 periods at 4% has a factor of $29.77808$.

$FV = 6000 \times 29.77808 = \$178\,668.48$.

Total contributions $= 6000 \times 20 = \$120\,000$, so the interest earned is $178\,668.48 - 120\,000 = \$58\,668.48$.

questions.question: Albert's account will have a future value of \$178 668.48 after 20 years. His bank has an account option that offers the same interest rate (4% p.a.), compounding quarterly rather than annually. Albert decides to open a new account and make quarterly contributions over a period of 10 years. How much would Albert need to contribute to the new account at the end of each quarter to achieve the same future value after 10 years? The table shows the future values of an annuity of \$1.
questions.answer:
Quarterly rate $= \dfrac{4\%}{4} = 1\%$ and the number of periods $= 10 \times 4 = 40$. From the table the factor is $48.88637$.

$$a \times 48.88637 = 178\,668.48 \Rightarrow a = \$3654.77.$$

questions.question:
The profit that a company makes in one month can be modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $P$ is the profit (in thousands of dollars) and $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Complete the table.

| Number of units produced (thousand) | 0 | 20 | 40 | 60 | 80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Profit (thousand \$) | 0 | | | | |

The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Graph the equation on the grid using the values $(0, 0)$, $(20, 800)$, $(40, 1200)$, $(60, 1200)$, $(80, 800)$.
questions.answer: Plot the five points and join them with a smooth, symmetrical, downwards-opening curve (a parabola) with its vertex at $(50, 1250)$.

questions.question: The profit of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$. State the name of this type of non-linear relationship.
questions.answer: A quadratic relationship (its graph is a parabola).

questions.question: The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). The profit is \$1200 thousand at both $n = 40$ and $n = 60$. Find how many units should be produced to maximise the company's monthly profits.
questions.answer: The maximum is on the axis of symmetry, which is midway between $n = 40$ and $n = 60$: $n = \dfrac{40 + 60}{2} = 50$. So $50\,000$ units should be produced.

questions.question: The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). What is the maximum profit that can be made per month?

The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Explain why the company should not try to produce 100 000 units of their product, justifying your response with calculations.
questions.answer: At $n = 100$: $P = 50(100) - 0.5(100)^2 = 5000 - 5000 = 0$. The company would make no profit at 100 000 units, which is less than it makes at lower production levels (maximum \$1 250 000 at 50 000 units).

questions.question: The area of a paddock is to be estimated. Due to thick spiky weeds through parts of the paddock, the surveyors are only able to find the measurements shown (parallel sides 122 m, 99 m, 108 m and 141 m, spaced 83 m, 152 m and 116 m apart respectively). Use three applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the paddock, in hectares, correct to 1 decimal place. (One hectare $= 10\,000\ \text{m}^2$.)

A paddock has an area of 3.9 hectares (3.93455 ha before rounding). A mixture of herbicide and fertiliser needs to be applied at a rate of 45 litres per hectare. How many litres of the mixture are needed for the paddock?
questions.answer: $3.9 \times 45 = 175.5$ L (or $3.93455 \times 45 \approx 177$ L using the unrounded area). Either answer is acceptable.

questions.question: A thunderstorm over a paddock of area $39\,345.5\ \text{m}^2$ sees the whole paddock receive 8 millimetres of rain. How much rain fell onto the paddock, correct to the nearest kilolitre?
questions.answer:
$V = Ah = 39\,345.5 \times 0.008 = 314.8\ \text{m}^3$.

Since $1\ \text{m}^3 = 1\ \text{kL}$, the rain was approximately $315$ kL.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed. The waiting time is less than 184 seconds 16% of the time and greater than 304 seconds 0.15% of the time. During the first three months of 2024, 4.16 million people visited the airport. If 30% of these people took a taxi from the airport, find the approximate number of people whose waiting time was greater than 184 seconds.
questions.answer:
$P(\text{wait} > 184) = 100\% - 16\% = 84\%$.

Number of people who took a taxi $= 0.30 \times 4\,160\,000 = 1\,248\,000$.

Number waiting more than 184 s $= 0.84 \times 1\,248\,000 = 1\,048\,320$ people.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed. The waiting time is less than 184 seconds 16% of the time and greater than 304 seconds 0.15% of the time. Determine the mean and standard deviation for the time spent waiting for a taxi at the airport.
questions.answer:
$16\%$ of the data lies below $z = -1$, so $184 = \mu - \sigma$. $0.15\%$ lies above $z = +3$, so $304 = \mu + 3\sigma$.

Subtracting: $304 - 184 = 4\sigma \Rightarrow \sigma = 30$ seconds. Then $\mu = 184 + 30 = 214$ seconds.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed with a mean of 214 seconds and a standard deviation of 30 seconds. Is it likely that the waiting time for a taxi will be two minutes or less? Justify your response with appropriate mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
Two minutes is $120$ seconds, so $z = \dfrac{120 - 214}{30} = -3.13$.

A $z$-score below $-3$ occurs with a probability of less than $0.15\%$, so it is very unlikely that the waiting time will be two minutes or less.
